intro: The fifty-second screen read 99 pictures, the set's 21 and 78 probes, with thirteen readers and four scorers: 1,074 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and one was misread. **63 of the 64 templates pass the legibility gate**, as in v0.54. The one that fails is `square_wheel` again, 0.938 in its eight pictures with the misread: the tier-4 playground's bicycle, in a part of the picture that is v0.54's to the pixel, was read as lying on its side, as v0.54's reader read it. **Every template that draws a figure on a seat reads 1.00**, and each of their 37 items has the score it had in v0.54's screen. Of the 28 items under full marks, twenty-three are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out, two are that bicycle's, two are half marks in the tier-4 street (the thief bird and the dropped ice cream) and one is a half mark on the stopped hose. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. Sixty-nine of the 99 pictures are v0.54's to the pixel, and of their 717 items 690 have the score they had; twenty-six of the 27 others are the clouds or a tree. The thirty pictures whose sitters were drawn again hold 385 items, and 371 have the score they had; ten of the 14 others are the clouds or a tree. The set's score is 0.972, for 0.974. On the strict count 52 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.54's 54. In the readers' unsure sections a sitter's legs, feet or seat are named in seven of the thirty pictures, for four in v0.54's screen: the man on the seesaw's low end, who reads as sitting on the grass to two readers of three, a sitter's legs in front of a bench in two pictures, and a child's feet off the ground in three.
design:
## Design tests

v0.55 draws the lower body of every seated figure again and changes no placement rule, so its whole-scene test is the bench (`vision/design_tests_v055.md`): eighteen of v0.54's pictures with a seated figure, each built again from its own record with the release's cast, with the same templates and the same people in the same places, and read both ways by twelve fresh readers with the screen's own prompt. I looked at the seated figures of thirty rebuilt pictures, cut out beside v0.54's, before any reader had one, and found nothing to mend.
- **That the figure sits:** in 36 readings of 36.
- **What the sitter does:** a reader reads in 12 of 12 and a sitter eats or drinks in 8 of 8.
- **The seat that is missing, and the heavy seesaw:** read in all four readings of each.
- **Anything new and odd about the legs:** a sitter's legs, feet or seat are in 6 unsure sections of 36, for 10 of 36 of v0.54's pictures, and no reader names a knee, a thigh or a shin as strange.

No picture was built again after a reading.
screen:
Across all 99 pictures 1,074 of 1,102 scored items had full marks, and one was misread (v0.54: 1,072 of 1,102, none). Of the 28 under full marks:
- twenty-three are setting items that five readers left out, sixteen the clouds and seven a tree, all zeros (v0.54 had twenty-six, from five readers). Two readers left the clouds out of six of their seven pictures;
- two are the square-wheeled bicycle's in the tier-4 playground, a half mark and a misread: "- Red bicycle, bottom right: lying on its side on the grass." and, among the unsure things, "- The bicycle seems to be lying flat/on its side — could be dropped by the boy pointing at the tree, or just parked oddly.";
- two are half marks in the tier-4 street, each a target beside another reading: "- The blue bird on the bench could be eating the woman's sandwich without her noticing (she is reading), or simply sitting next to food." and "- The ice cream could have been dropped by the girl or the dog could have caused it; either way she is upset.";
- one is the stopped hose of the tier-4 garden, a half mark: "- The hose: no water is visible coming out; it could be because the dog is standing on it, or she may simply not have turned it on. She is looking at the nozzle as if puzzled."

The set's headline is all items 0.972 (0.974 in v0.54). Of its 286 items ten are under full marks: the clouds in four pictures and a tree in one (things 0.954), the bicycle's two (contradictions 0.946) and the three half marks (inferences 0.953). Actions read 1.00.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.56 is `vision/flaws_v055.md`.

**The seated figures.** Thirty pictures hold a figure on a seat, a swing, a seesaw or a slide, and all thirty have v0.54's templates and people in v0.54's places with the sitter drawn again. The seven templates that draw one read 1.00 in three or four pictures each, as in v0.54, and their 37 items have each the score they had. The figure that sits on nothing: "- The old man appears to be sitting on nothing; there is no chair, stool or bench under him. This looks impossible / unintentionally strange (or a missing chair)." What the readers doubted is in their unsure sections, which name a sitter's legs, feet or seat in seven of the thirty pictures, for four of the same thirty in v0.54's screen. Two of the seven are the man on the seesaw's low end, in two of his three pictures: "- The man seems to sit almost on the grass at the end of the seesaw rather than clearly on the seat; could be read as sitting on the ground holding the end down." Two are a sitter's legs in front of a bench, which v0.54's reader of one of them wrote too: "- The boy's legs come forward off the front of the bench; seated pose looks a little awkward but fine." Three are a child's feet off the ground. No reader names a knee, a thigh, a shin or a seat as strange. The bench before the screen, where the same readers read both ways, had fewer doubts with the new legs (6 readings of 36 for 10); the screen, with one reader a picture, has more (7 for 4). Both counts are small, and both leave the same two things for the next list: the low rider's seat, and a bench drawn shallower than a sitter's thigh is long.

**The square wheel.** Eight pictures, four of the wheelbarrow and four of the bicycle. The four barrows and three bicycles read in full; one barrow's wheel, named only among the unsure things by v0.54's reader, is in this reader's description. The tier-4 playground's bicycle was read as lying on its side, as in v0.54, by another reader, and this scorer marked the explain item a misread where v0.54's gave a zero. Over three screens and a bench that bicycle has been read six times: its wheels are square in the description twice, among the unsure things once, and not named three times. No other bicycle is read so. It stands in the front corner of the picture with the most events.

**A second reading of the pictures that came back, and a first of those that changed.** Sixty-nine of the 99 pictures are v0.54's to the pixel, thirteen of the set and 56 probes, and they hold 717 items. Item for item against v0.54's screen, 690 have the same score, fourteen are higher and thirteen lower; twenty-six of the 27 are the clouds or a tree, and the other is that wheelbarrow's wheel. The thirty pictures with a sitter drawn again hold 385 items: 371 have the same score, eight are higher and six lower; ten of the 14 are the clouds or a tree, and the other four are the bicycle's two items and the street's two half marks. None is an item of a seated figure.

**The cast in the descriptions.** By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the four grown figures of v0.49's count are called by a young name first in 3 of their 81 pictures, for 4 of 81 in v0.54: the woman in purple in 1 of 25, the woman in the yellow dress in 1 of 21, the man in the red shirt in 1 of 19 and the man in green in none of 16. They are v0.54's three pictures again, each by another reader: the man walking with a book, the woman in the yellow dress sitting on nothing with a drink, and the woman in purple raking. The man in the red shirt is a man in all three pictures where he sits. His moustache is in his line in 2 of his 19 pictures (5 of 19 in v0.54), and the beard of the man in green in 11 of his 16 (12 of 16).

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers listed 85 full marks as judgement calls, for 82 in v0.54. In 48 the target stands beside another reading (42 in v0.54), and in 37 a near word or a target partly said was credited (40), twenty of them a word for a person. With the 48 halved, twelve templates are under 0.9, and 52 of the 64 pass (54 in v0.54); with all 85 halved, 42 pass (44). The four scorers listed 20, 28, 14 and 23, so the strict counts compare only roughly.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 38 oddities in the 99 pictures, 0.4 a picture as in v0.54, and 12 of them in the set for 8. The readers' remarks were 2.44 per picture (2.71). What the oddities are about: figures over the pond's near edge, in four pictures; the man on the seesaw's low end, in two; a sitter's legs in front of a bench, in two; hoses, in three; and singles. Four are about an animal: a goat in a park, a bird a boy runs at, a bird large on a lamp and a puppy lying on a hose that still runs.
redrawn: The seven templates that draw a figure on a seat (`read_bench`, `drink_bench`, `sitting_on_air`, `seesaw_heavy`, `seesaw`, `swing`, `slide`) read 1.00, as they did, with every sitter drawn again. `ice_cream` and `dog_begs`, whose eater often sits, read 1.00 as well. `bird_steals`, whose reader sits beside the sandwich, reads 0.967 in five pictures: a half mark, and five full marks beside the same other reading, a bird that only sits next to the food. `square_wheel` reads 0.938 with one misread and is under the gate, on a bicycle that was not drawn again. `blocked_hose` reads 0.975 and `ice_cream_drop` 0.982, a half mark each. `water_upward` and `dog_wants_walk` read 1.00 and are under 0.9 on the strict count a third screen running. It is one screen, of 3 to 28 items a template, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.17.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (33 in three, 8 in four, 16 in five, 2 in six, and one each in seven, eight, ten, thirteen and sixteen). 63 of 64 pass, as in v0.54; 64 did in v0.53 and 63 in v0.52. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. Four templates are under 1.00: `square_wheel` (0.938 on twenty-four items in eight pictures, one misread), which fails on the misread, `bird_steals` (0.967 on fifteen items in five pictures), `blocked_hose` (0.975 on twenty items in five pictures) and `ice_cream_drop` (0.982 on twenty-eight items in seven pictures); the other 60 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v055/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 48 full marks that stand beside another reading halved, 52 of the 64 pass. The square wheel's failure is one bicycle's, in a picture whose bicycle did not change: read as lying on its side by two readers running, and scored two zeros by one scorer and a half and a misread by the next. The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
calib: Six of the calibration's 252 numbers moved by 0.002 or more, where none had in v0.54, all on the two templates whose seated figure is measured: `seesaw_heavy`'s inference (its mean from 0.233 to 0.213 and its salience from -0.687 to -0.651) and the two contradiction items of `sitting_on_air` (their means by 0.017 and their salience from 0.072 to 0.106). By these numbers three priors, which keep two places, would change: `seesaw_heavy`'s from -0.69 to -0.65, `sitting_on_air`'s from 0.07 to 0.11, and `about_to_trip`'s from 0.14 to 0.15 on the rounding edge v0.54 found. **All three were left at v0.54's.** With the two new priors the planner drew another plan for the tier-3 playground on its seed, a lost balloon where v0.54 has the walker about to trip, and the probes, which fill each template's count from what the set holds, then drew other events in most of their pictures: the screen would have read a new set, not v0.54's with its sitters drawn again. With v0.54's priors all sixteen cells and the five isomorphs have v0.54's templates on v0.54's seeds, and so do the 78 probes. Every record's predicted difficulty is computed from the new calibration, and every cell is in its band by it. A release that changes the set should take the three priors. The calibration was measured once, with the cast as it is released (`tools/cycle/calib_cmp.py`).
inspection: Every cell of the set was built under revision 49 with the new cast. The twelve cells of tiers 1 to 3 placed on their showcase seeds, the tier-4 park on the v0.43 seed, the tier-4 street on v0.49's, on its twenty-second step, and the tier-4 playground on v0.53's base, on its seventh step, each with v0.54's templates and v0.54's people; the tier-4 garden is v0.46's set forced on v0.46's seed, as in v0.53 and v0.54 (`tools/cycle/forced_cell.py`). Thirteen of the 21 pictures, three of the five isomorphs among them, are v0.54's to the pixel; the other eight differ in their sitter alone. The probe pass built 61 and left one template short, the begging dog; two small forced groups filled it, the pass stratified by angle added 12, and three more were forced for the wheelbarrow (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 78 probes with v0.54's names, 47 gardens, 23 parks, 6 playgrounds and 2 streets, 56 of them v0.54's to the pixel and the other 22 differing in their sitters alone. In all 99 no element is more than 12 units from where v0.54 has it. **I looked at the part of each of the thirty pictures that changed, beside v0.54's, before any reader had them, found nothing to mend, and built none again after that look.** All 99 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 355 of 355. Its soft palette warning is raised by 313 records, for 314 in v0.54, with the median share of a figure's pixels on a palette colour as it was, 0.88. The target was not loosened.
